notes.title: Dev Log: Hub Tech & Pacification Protocols
notes.content:
[h3]Brute force wasn’t enough. Humanity didn’t just need to match the Nexera in firepower - it needed to [b]outpace[/b] them in deployment.[/h3][p]That’s where the [b]IPE’s Hub Technology[/b] came in.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/46bcc6a2790f7c813fab515e08a213d78faeace1.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]The Command Hub: Instant Power, Zero Humans[/h2][p]The [b]Command Hub[/b] is the crown jewel of IPE engineering.[/p][p]Dropped from orbit into a designated safe zone (or [i]cleared[/i] zone, if needed), the hub is [b]fully energy-autonomous[/b]. Over 60% of its structure is made up of a self-contained [b]nuclear core[/b], capable of powering up to [b]50,000 connected hubs[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/7ae054af617ca771c92403b805062037d3e1a1b6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]But its true marvel lies in the way it distributes energy:
Through compressed, focused [b]energy beams[/b], the Command Hub can power remote structures instantly - no wires, no personnel, no contact required.[/p][p][/p][p]If no safe landing zone is available, the IPE sends an advance shuttle filled with [b]Guardian units[/b] to secure a perimeter before Hub deployment begins.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]Hubs: Plug-and-Play Outposts[/h2][p]Once the Command Hub is active, [b]Hubs[/b] are launched from orbit like needles, piercing the ground to establish instant outposts.[/p][p]These are not temporary shelters. Each Hub is designed to:[/p][list][*][p]Provide [b]food, shelter, and weapons[/b] for up to [b]7 personnel[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Sustain them for [b]10 days[/b] without external supply[/p][/*][*][p]Operate immediately with zero setup time[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/bbefb25cb0a91aa2ec0a5e94e6dbda01a0796500.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The IPE can drop and activate dozens of these Hubs in minutes, forming the backbone of a colony or battlefield deployment zone.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h2]T.F.L. Technology: Bending Time, Not Breaking It[/h2][p]During the development of the Hub system, IPE researchers discovered something unexpected.[/p][p]By [b]focusing and condensing energy[/b], they found they could [i]manipulate gravity[/i] in extremely localized fields — which, in turn, affected [b]time[/b].[/p][p]This led to the creation of [b]T.F.L. (Time Focus Loop) zones[/b]:
Areas where time is drastically slowed down in a confined space. The effect isn’t strong enough to reverse time — but it’s powerful enough to allow buildings to be [b]modified or constructed in mere seconds[/b].[/p][p]Using T.F.L. tech, an IPE operator can establish a fully operational base faster than ever thought possible. For the Nexera, this was the turning point.
For the rest of the galaxy… it became a warning.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/0977e4383b3da413c967192324279b53a1cb3e60.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][b]Space Tales[/b] launches into Early Access on [b]October 22. [/b]Until then, stay tuned for more lore, tech deep-dives, and unit breakdowns.

[url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2457960/Space_Tales/"]WISHLIST NOW[/url][/p]

notes.title: Dev Log – Galactic Field Guide, Vol. 1
notes.content:
[h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/30a41b25dad4adf28927683f7e0336d292bd4dac.jpg"][/img][b]

XV-22[/b] — [i]“The Dry Grave”[/i] | [b]Campaign Chapter 1[/b][/h3][p]
A sun-blasted rock of red sand, wind-carved stone, and half-buried Kel Tan ruins. XV-22 was useful to the IPE only as a refuel pit - until a transport carrying a [i]classified Nexera sample[/i] crash-landed here. When a Nester emerged to claim the cargo, HQ called in Commander Xander. Expect: scarce resources, ancient puzzles, and the first Wanderer boss lurking in the dust.[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]

[/b][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/b0f5f82cbe40560e3365cff2bac0a7e9f71547a2.png"][/img][/h3][p][/p][h3][b]Wangor[/b] — [i]“The Painted Sentinel”[/i] | [b]Chapter 2[/b][/h3][p]At first glance: emerald hills, cobalt rivers, rainbow mountains. Reality: oxidized copper soils where only hardy fungi grow. Wangor sits on the fringe of Kel Tan space - an early-warning post the aliens guard jealously. Xander’s father discovered the planet (and paid the price). Now secret IPE labs tunnel beneath those “pretty” ridges…and the Killbots are waiting.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/2f6e96bec5072c873937aa3686fdcd9cc5b73add.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Afalee[/b] — [i]“Garden Turned Grave”[/i] | [b]Chapter 3[/b][/h3][p]One of humanity’s twin Edens after Earth. Fresh water, fertile fields, towering eco-cities. Afalee resisted the IPE—until the Nexera threat forced cooperation. But Capso’s Despot unleashed a bioweapon, spawning the Necroborg and plunging the bread-basket of the galaxy into nightmare. You’ll arrive after the fall, fighting through overgrown streets and twisted bio-steel forests.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/7451b00b536cb89d1507834d5755bc6c1a9b62a5.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Capso[/b] — [i]“Forge World of the Despot”[/i] | [b]Chapter 4[/b][/h3][p]Heavy gravity, metallic deserts, and the beating heart of IPE industry. A dormant Nester slumbered in Capso’s core—until war bombs woke it, shearing away a third of the planet. The scar became a megacity and IPE capital; the caverns below churn out fleets, suits, and weapons. Soil imported from Afalee grows token greenery under domes, but make no mistake: this is a world of smoke, steel, and secrets.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h2]What This Means for Gameplay[/h2][list][*][p][b]Unique Biomes & Resources:[/b] From Wangor’s copper fungi to Capso’s high-gravity ore, every planet alters your economy and tactics.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Faction-Driven Missions:[/b] Nexera swarms on XV-22, Killbot bastions on Wangor, Necroborg infestations on Afalee... each chapter is practically a new game mode.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Lore Clues Everywhere:[/b] Scan ruins, decode logs, and piece together how the IPE, Kel Tan, and Nexera destinies collide.[/p][/*][/list][p]Wish-list [b]Space Tales[/b] if you haven’t already, and hop into Discord to tell us which world you’re most eager (or terrified) to visit![/p]

notes.title: Bio-Files, Part 2
notes.content:
[h2]1. Spitter – [i]“The Acid Gut”[/i][/h2][p]When Larvae sniff you out and Squids chew up the front line, [b]Spitters[/b] arrive to finish the meal. They spread across hard surfaces, coating walls and rocks in a viscous acid that “pre-digests” metal and flesh for easy Nester absorption.[/p][list][*][p][b]In-Game Behavior:[/b] Sets up corrosive pools that eat structures over time.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Counterplay:[/b] High-burst damage or captured monsters with splash are your best bet—kill them before your defenses melt.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/585181277aa5766506852813400ad9ab0808e706.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]2. Crawler – [i]“The Bone-Plated Battering Ram”[/i][/h2][p]If Squids bounce off reinforced walls, the Nester sends in [b]Crawlers[/b]. Built from dense bone lattice, they’re slower but far tougher, shrugging off small-arms fire while smashing fortifications.[/p][list][*][p][b]In-Game Behavior:[/b] Tanky siege unit that targets walls first, forces you to diversify damage types.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Counterplay:[/b] Armor-piercing turrets, artillery, or your own captured Brute will crack that shell.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/d87d3ed2e74c8f58df67f140a1bfb47a53fe6b39.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]3. Jumper – [i]“The Wall-Hopper”[/i][/h2][p]Decades of IPE defense lines taught the Nexera a new trick: [b]Jumpers[/b]. These winged assassins vault any obstacle and dive straight for high-priority targets—usually your recruits’ faces.[/p][list][*][p][b]In-Game Behavior:[/b] Leaps over terrain, ignores choke points, focuses on infantry.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Counterplay:[/b] Long-range fire or heavily armored mechs; keep AA turrets near vital squads.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/ac031b06f47aef67e1834dffd41f13e30194c9dc.jpg"][/img]
[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]4. Drifter – [i]“The Living Railgun”[/i][/h2][p]Only five years old in the evolutionary timeline, [b]Drifters[/b] may contain human DNA. Early reports guessed they were tactical overseers; autopsies reveal that most of their neural energy is repurposed into [b]destructive energy waves[/b].[/p][list][*][p][b]In-Game Behavior:[/b] Charges up line-beam attacks that one-shot light units and fry electronics.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Counterplay:[/b] Disrupt with stuns or spread your army to minimize beam lanes; capture attempts are… ill-advised (for now).

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/977b09ff63bd9b7d0ae30d5ad96de5f913a9671f.jpg"][/img]

[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]What’s Next?
[/h3][p]These four units debut in our next Nexera planet mission alongside new AI behaviors and counter tools. Your feedback from the Wargame Fest demo helped shape their stats - keep those reports coming in [b]Discord[/b] so we can fine-tune the swarm!
[/p][p]Haven’t wish-listed [b]Space Tales[/b] yet? Smash that green button and share with a friend - your click makes the IPE accountants smile :) :)[/p][p]
[b]The Saigon Dragon Studios Team[/b][/p]

notes.title: Bio-Files: The Nexera Threat
notes.content:
[h2]1. Where It All Began — The Dormant Doom
[/h2][p]The Nexera were unknown — [b]asleep and buried somewhere in our galaxy [/b]— until their first, terrifying awakening on Capso during the Afalee-Wangor interplanetary war. They are [b]not pests[/b]; they’re an unstoppable force that consumes entire worlds, showing zero empathy … even toward their own biomass.
[/p][p]A Nexera “civilization” doesn’t really exist. Instead, individual [b]Nesters[/b] crash-land, bury themselves, and convert anything they touch into new, deadlier forms. They don’t reproduce conventionally; they [b]clone[/b] shards of themselves (Nestroids) before the host planet dies, seeding more worlds with fragments of annihilation. Why evolve if you only clone? Why lie dormant on thriving planets? Every answer just leads to bigger questions—and greater dread.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/ea450cfa159d27452f241542b2427a36f0e1d2b6.jpg"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h2]2. The Nester — Brain, Belly, & Battlefield Genius
[/h2][p]Every Nexera life-cycle starts - and ends- with a [b]Nester[/b]. It may arrive as small as an insect, yet the genetic blueprint inside can sculpt a planet-devouring titan. In the absence of threats, the Nester quietly grows and spawns Nestroids. But if resistance appears, its tactical brilliance ignites: it calculates the exact biomass needed, fabricates perfect counters, and sends them out in ruthless waves.
[/p][p]One comfort? A Nester never survives the landing: it either devours the planet or dies trying. Unfortunately, history shows they hit their target more often than not.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/00b2bbc29178b4f49ee09da362582dd360cc904c.jpg"][/img]
[/p][hr][/hr][h2]3. Larva — The Nose of the Hive
[/h2][p]Originally misidentified as juvenile Nexera, [b]Larvae[/b] are actually the Nester’s roaming olfactory system. Able to burrow through soil and creep across the surface, they sniff out nutrients, soft ground, and - most annoyingly - [b]your base[/b]. Kill them early, or watch them map a perfect invasion route for the tentacles to follow.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/f8245f93166938c801916e23459263d21adc07d7.jpg"][/img]
[/p][hr][/hr][h2]4. Squid — The Disposable Blade
[/h2][p]Need destruction on a budget? The Nester spawns [b]Squids[/b]: eight-tentacled maws packed with serrated teeth but no stomach. They don’t eat; they [b]pulverize[/b]. After a target is shredded, a Squid hauls the debris (and its own biomass) back to the Nester, fusing into the main body and accelerating growth. Sending human troops against Squids only feeds the enemy, so the IPE now prefers robotic front lines. Even so, nothing feels safe when you hear their screech in the mist.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/d87d3ed2e74c8f58df67f140a1bfb47a53fe6b39.jpg"][/img]
[/p][hr][/hr][h3]Next Steps & Demo Update
[/h3][p]Your feedback from Gameverse HCMC is already shaping a small Nexera balance patch: tweaked Larva scouting frequency, clearer Squid audio cues, and an early look at the Nester boss UI. Keep the reports coming in [url="https://discord.gg/mej9QXyvj5"]Discord[/url]; every note helps us fine-tune the swarm.
[/p][p]If you haven’t yet, [b]wishlist Space Tales[/b] and tell a friend... your clicks help our signal cut through the void![/p][p]Until next time: stay sharp, watch the mist, and never underestimate an insect-sized meteor.[/p][p]
[b]—The Saigon Dragon Studios Team[/b][/p]

notes.title: Gameverse HCMC Recap – Xin Chào & Thank You!
notes.content:
Hi Commanders,

We’re back from Gameverse in Ho Chi Minh City, and we want to thank everyone who stopped by the booth to try the newest Space Tales demo. Your time, feedback, and good vibes were priceless!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/aab934d728ac42a7839745e540cfc2a58d0d835d.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] What Happened on the Show Floor 
[/list]
- Hands-on Demo: Players tested our reworked Campaign missions and the updated Survival Map.
- Plush Giveaway: Every Nexera plush we brought found a new home - congrats to the winners!
- Live Feedback: Dozens of notes on mission pacing, Survival difficulty, and Hub usability.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/43af36c991144f40aaca86a9f8559a0a6e916d9d.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] Key Takeaways
[/list]

Here are the four main points we pulled from your feedback —and what we’re doing about each one:

Campaign flow. Most of you felt the early objectives are clearer now, but a few sections could still use extra guidance. We’re adding minor tweaks to mission prompts and tutorial pop-ups to smooth those rough spots.

Survival mode. The new map layout got a thumbs-up, though many of you said the first waves still hit a bit too hard, too fast (especially in Hard mode). We’re stretching the early wave timers so the difficulty ramps more gradually.

Hub transformations. The eight new Hub forms were a clear highlight, yet a couple of icons left players scratching their heads. We’re polishing those UI assets. 

[list]
[*] Next on the Roadmap
[/list]
- Demo Patch (probably late June) – Balance tweaks, UI polish, and bug fixes based on Gameverse feedback.
- Necroborg Preview – First screenshots & info on our third faction.


[list]
[*] Stay Involved
[/list]
[url=https://discord.gg/mej9QXyvj5]Discord[/url]: Drop additional feedback or bug reports any time

[b]Wishlist: If you enjoyed the demo, please wishlist Space Tales on Steam—it really helps with visibility.
[/b]

Thank you again to everyone who played, chatted, or just stopped by to say hi. Your support keeps the project moving forward at warp speed!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/1d112f1749c103db702f6fa8dbbf30a8e08eb66c.jpg[/img]

The Saigon Dragon Studios Team

notes.title: Dev Update – Monster Capture Deep Dive
notes.content:
Well, in Space Tales you can make that dream a reality! Today we’re giving more info about our Monster Capture & Training system: one of the features we’re most excited to share.


[b]1. Why Capture?[/b]
[list]
[*] Game-changer units: Boss-level creatures come with unique abilities  that standard troops can’t match.
[/list][list]
[*] Flexible strategies: Need a frontline tank? A long-range disrupter? Different monsters fill different roles.
[/list][list]
[*] Bragging rights: Nothing says “Commander Supreme” like turning yesterday’s terror into tomorrow’s mascot.
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/RAGeAxM.gif[/img]


[b]2. How It Works[/b]

[list]
[*] Scout & Weaken: Neutral Monsters roam each planet. Whittle their health down— the lower it is, the greater your capture odds.
[/list][list]
[*] Deploy Capture Beacons: Click the Capture icon (you get three attempts per Monster). 
[/list][list]
[*] Success or Escape: A successful tether drops the beast into a stasis field for transport. Failure? It breaks free and you’ll need to regroup - or risk a very angry counter-attack.
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/4gs3Gdw.gif[/img]

[b]3. Laboratory[/b]
Back at base, use the Laboratory to level up your monster!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44300472/242cd370c5044d476ba8e38799c2c604a6d09d77.jpg[/img]

[b]4. What’s Next?[/b]
We’re polishing animations, SFX, and UI feedback (tutorial on how to capture monsters). Your feedback from the Wargame Fest demo has been invaluable - keep 'em coming!


[b]5. Join the Conversation[/b]
Hop into our [url=https://discord.gg/mej9QXyvj5]Discord [/url]to share capture stories, balance ideas, or monster concepts you’d love to see. And if you haven’t already, please wishlist Space Tales — it helps us reach more strategy fans and keeps the alien wrangling funded!

Thanks for reading, and happy hunting! Gotta Catch em All ! :D


—The Saigon Dragon Studios Team
